indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.initialization: let mut index = 0; block.resize_with(values.len(), || { let value = values[index]; index += 1; value });
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.hypothesis: Reserving once through resize_with rather than extending an iterator may remove per-element capacity-check overhead while retaining the final representation copy.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.paired_order: Six alternating process pairs, extend first and indexed resize second; no agent-initiated build overlapped samples, host otherwise uncontrolled.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.conclusion: Indexed resize median was about 34.4 ms versus 38.9 ms for extend in these samples, with overlapping ranges. This does not establish the cause or eliminate the previously observed raw-copy performance gap; the raw baseline was not rerun in this paired trial.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.disposition: Rejected as sufficient evidence for migration; trial source reverted to the pre-trial safe candidate. No implementation committed or pushed.

compatibility_constraint: The existing helper explicitly promises complete object-representation copying. Both candidates finish with standard slice copy_from_slice, documented as memcpy in the pinned Rust source; value-only iteration does not establish padding preservation.
dependency_finding: allocator-api2 0.4.0 Vec::extend_from_slice uses iter().cloned(), so it cannot preserve the observable custom-Clone bypass contract
limitations: Only three timing samples per candidate
Microbenchmark rather than end-to-end CAD workload
status: Continue investigation; both safe representation-preserving candidates have measured helper overhead
